text:
Mattias Samuelsson has become the defenseman Buffalo leans on most: 23.71 minutes a night on the season, and 25.13 over the last ten games, nearly four more than before. The Philadelphia-born second-round pick from 2018 has two goals and nine points in 16 games with no power-play points at all, which tells you the offense is coming at even strength.

Evolving-Hockey ranked him 20th among 215 defensemen last season at 2.4 wins above replacement, most of it from even-strength offense, so this isn't a surprise run. His scoring rate sits inside his talent range, and his own shooting is roughly normal.

The 5v5 numbers are just about even: 51 percent of shot attempts, 48.5 percent of expected goals, slightly worse than without him. That's the cost of facing harder minutes. NHL EDGE has him in the 90th percentile for top speed and 88th for shot speed, which is a rare combination for a big defenseman. Our range has him around 47 points.
headline: Samuelsson is Buffalo's minute-eater now
